# Lab #3: Avengers

## Overview

In this lab, we are going to

1. Reshape a data set
2. Use the data to fact-check some statistics in a published report. 

The deliverable is, again, a team-edited report. You will do this in your GitHub repository for Lab #3 in Classroom 50. As before, you will be editing the `qmd` file and pushing it to the repo. Your repo is set up to automatically render this to the `md` file. **Do not edit the `md` file directly!**

The overall aim of this lab is to tidy a data set, then use it for fact-checking a report.


## Data Background

In a universe where time travel, alternate lifelines, and portals with all kinds of powers exist, dying might be less permanent than in the world that we are used to. 

The data were collected by Walt Hickey at FiveThirtyEight in 2015. This time we are interested in a review of life and death among the Avengers, a group of super heroes in the Marvel universe; the accompanying article is archived [here](https://web.archive.org/web/20150512194216/http://fivethirtyeight.com/features/avengers-death-comics-age-of-ultron/), and the description of the data is [here](https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/tree/master/avengers).

We can access the resulting data using the command:

```{r}
avengers <- read.csv("https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/raw/refs/heads/master/avengers/avengers.csv")
head(avengers)
```


## What you need to do

### As a team: data tidying

The avenger data consists of ten columns for each avenger called Death[1-5] to Return[1-5].

1. Get the data into a format where the five columns for Death[1-5] are replaced by two columns: Time, and Death. 
    * Time should be a number between 1 and 5 (look into the function `parse_number`)
    * Death is a categorical variables with values "YES", "NO" and "". 
    * Call the resulting data set `deaths`. (Note: you can filter out `""`, the empty strings, from this result.)

2. Similarly, deal with the returns of characters. Call this dataset `returns`.

3. Based on these datasets:
    * What is the average number of deaths an Avenger suffers?
    * What is the average number of returns an Avenger has?


### Individually (recording in shared document): fact checking

4. Choose one of the statements in the [article](https://web.archive.org/web/20150512194216/http://fivethirtyeight.com/features/avengers-death-comics-age-of-ultron/) and fact check it based on the data. 
    * Use `dplyr` functionality whenever possible.
    * Upload the claim, code to check the claim, and your response to the repository. Make sure to include your name with the claim you chose.
    * Discuss and refine answers as a team.

## Remember the GitHub steps

1. Open a [git repository in Positron](https://positron.posit.co/git.html#open-a-git-repository) from the existing git repository for the assignment
    A) New > New Folder from Git 
    A) In "Repository URL", past the URL of your group's GitHub repository. You can find this under the `<>Code` button; just copy the `HTTPS` URL.
    A) Set the parent folder to be the folder you created for this class.
    A) Select "OK"

1. In Positron, modify the `README.qmd` file as you complete the assignment.
    * Make sure to check for and sync changes often! This will avoid major commit issues later.

1. Stage changes
    A) Select "Source Control" in the left pane (looks like a branch)
    A) Under "Changes", select the `+` to stage changes. (Only stage the `qmd` file!)

1. Commit changes to your local repo. 
    A) Add a commit message above the blue commit button
    A) Select "Commit"

1. Sync changes: once you have done a commit, select "Sync Changes". This will push changes and pull new changes from others.
    * Errors? Do a separate pull action, resolve merge changes, then repeat.
